DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 104 s. 2022 September 28, 2022 HON. RAUL E. TABIRARA Municipal Mayor Pandan, Catanduanes Dear Hon. Tabirara: This pertains to your letter dated 13 July 2022 on a query whether a non-winning candidate in the recent election may be hired as a consultant or job order employee. The antecedent facts are as follows I 2. 3. 4. 5. The letter cited Section 4, Rule XIII, Omnibus Rules on Appointment and Other Personnel Action (CSC Memorandum Circular No. 40, s. 1998 as amended) which provides that: Sec. 4. A person who lost in an election (except Barangay election) should not be eligible for appointment or reappointment to any office of the government or any government owned or controlled corporation within one (1) year following such election. The interpretation presented by the letter sender is that the above cited provision only applies to appointive positions in any office of the government or any government owned and controlled corporation. As such, it was concluded that the same does not apply to consultant or job order personnel as they are not considered engaged in government services. CSC Resolution No. 01-1606, dated 4 October 2001 cited in the letter allegedly ratiocinated that the purpose of the prohibition is not defeated when a non- winning candidate is hired as consultant considering that the services of a consultant are not directly delivered to the people who rejected him/her, but more to the person who hires him/her. Likewise mentioned is the DILG 13 Legal Opinion No. 2016-032 dated 29 September 2016 which stated that hiring on job order basis of non-winning candidates in an election may be allowed citing as its basis CSC Memorandum Circular No. 38, s. 1993 (now reproduced under Rule XI, Omnibus Rules on Appointment and Other Personnel Action/CSC Memorandum Circular No. 40, s. 1998) Finally, based on the foregoing submission, the concerned local chief executive "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline NO.: 8876-34-54

6. is asking for the permission of the DILG Regional Office for the hiring of a non- winning candidate as a consultant or on a job order basis. In requesting for the DILG Central Office's position on the subject matter, the Regional Office submitted its position quoting its draft response for this level's evaluation. It was anchored on a most recent resolution of the CSC that: "the hiring on the job-order basis of non-winning candidates in an election is tantamount to circumvention of the Civil Service Law and rules, particularly the rule prohibiting the appointment of a person who lost in an election within one year following such election". In relation to CSC Resolution No. 1100267, DILG Opinion No. 62 s. 2018 was likewise cited as follows: Although services rendered under Job Order contracts are not considered government services as there is no employer- employee relationship created between the government and the job order employee, the compensation received out of the contract is sourced from government funds" Thus, its final position is that the responsibility of the person who hires a non- winning candidate as a consultant to pay his/her salary and should not be taken from the public fund. We respectfully agree on the position taken by the DILG Regional Office, albeit on a more bolstered position and legal basis as hereinbelow discussed. We trace the One (I) year government employment ban for losing candidates from a constitutional prohibition expressed under Section 6, Article IX-B, of the 1987 Philippine Constitution, stated as follows: "Section 6. No candidate who has lost in any election shall, within one year after such election, be appointed to any office in the government or any government-owned or controlled corporations or in any of their subsidiaries. " Consistent with the afore-cited constitutional provision, R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991", echoed in this provision: Section 94. xxx ; Candidates Who Lost in an Election (a) Xxx (b) Except for losing candidates in barangay elections, no candidate who lost in any election shall, within one (1) year after such election, be appointed to any office in the government or any government-owned or controlled corporations or in any of their subsidiaries. It bears stressing that the rationale behind the one (1) year government employment prohibition of losing candidates finds its way to a certain degree of respect of the electorate's voice rejecting the offer of the losing candidate to serve the public. This rationale is constitutionally cemented by no less than the state principle enshrined under Section 1, Article II, of the 1987 Philippine Constitution, viz: SECTION I. The Philippines is a democratic and republican State.

Sove?eignty resides in the people and all government authority emanates from them. Thus, if a public service offer from a candidate was rejected by the electorate through a concluded popular election, it is the people speaking of withholding any other authority that the government may extend towards the losing candidate, its platform and the influence he/she may affect to governmental operations. It is from the concept of the electorate's withholding of governmental authority that the prohibition in the utilization of public funds for the payment of salaries in favor of losing candidates may have been conceptualized. Going further, this is equally and precisely the rationale behind the rule on automatic resignation of appointive officials upon filing of Certificate of Candidacy — to avoid any influence the candidate may affect to the governmental operations pending the decision of the electorate on whether or not to accept his/her political direction/contemplated governmental reforms/platform Now, therefore, if losing candidates will be permitted to serve the public other than through the elective position, immediately after losing said election, then the electorate's reasons/bases for not electing said candidate will be negated, thus the voice of the electorate overridden. Such will become a blatant disregard of being a democratic and republican state. To readily avoid said occurrence, the constitution explicitly provided a prohibition of one (1) year in order to balance the matter with the state's protection of individual's right to seek for employment. Evidently, however, it is the constitution dictating that the voice of the people is of paramount importance. Having traced and laid the rationale of the constitutional prohibition being the utmost respect towards the voice of the people in withholding their trust and confidence from the losing candidates, it follows that an interpretation that limits the prohibition to appointive positions alone will not give justice to the legislative intent behind the constitutional prohibition. To put it squarely, if the prohibition applies to appointive positions wherein appointees are under the disciplining authority of government agencies as well as the Civil Service Commission (CSC), all the more that the prohibition should strictly apply to those who are not within said disciplining authorities wherein the government's only hold is a mere contract of services and its only remedy is termination of contract. Verily, we don't see any cogent reason not to construe the word "appointed" in the phrase "appointed to any office in the government or any government-owned or controlled corporations or in any of their subsidiaries" in a generic sense, so as to cover those under contract of service or Job Order (J.O.) status, if such legal construction will give life and meaning to the legislative intent of the constitutional prohibition. To construe otherwise will make a subtle way of circumventing the pertinent constitutional prohibition. This, we may not allow following the principle that what is directly prohibited may not be indirectly allowed. Insofar as the other resolutions of the CSC is concerned cited by letter send, may we clarify that in stating that the same applies to appointive position, the commission is referring to the Omnibus Rules on Appointment and Other Personnel Action, which clearly applies to government employees alone. It is the said commission's policy lifted from, or pursuant to, the constitutional prohibition. Thus, it cannot be faulted when it interpreted the policy according the scope and coverage thereof which extend only to employees in the government service. Thus, it is correct in stating that the assailed provision in the Omnibus Rules on Appointment and Other Personnel Action (CSC Memorandum Circular No. 40, s. 1998).

It cannot either be claimed that the more recent CSC Resolution, CSC Resolution No. 1100267 dated 15 February 2011, which states: "the hirinq on the iob-order basis of non-winninq candidates in an election is tantamount to circumvent the Civil Service Law and rules. particularlv the rule prohibitinq the appointment of a person who lost in an election within one year following such election", contradicted its previous resolutions, because it did not. The use of the terms "tantamount to" ("equivalent to") in the afore-qouted CSC Resolution did not apply directly the Omnibus Rules on Appointment and Other Personnel Action, it merely applied "by analogy" said policy to the case of contract of service or J.O. personnel. Finally, we resolve that the One-Year Ban for candidates who lost in the election set forth under Section 94 (b) of the Local Government Code that was lifted from the constitutional prohibition expressed under Section 6, Article IX-B, of the 1987 Philippine Constitution, applies to the act of hiring through Contract of Service (COS) or Job Order (J.O.) status or arrangement. May we stipulate that the foregoing opinion supersedes any contrary opinion previously issued by the DILG Regional Offices as the same may have been anchored to previous CSC Resolutions which are confined to the extent and coverage of relevant CSC Memorandum Circulars. Nonetheless, the foregoing opinion IS issued without prejudice to any contrary ruling and/or interpretation by competent courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Ve rul yours, BY AUT ORITY OF THE SECRETARY: TY. JUAN ICTOR R. LLAMAS nde ecretary for External and Legislative Affairs OUSELA/JVRULRALLD/kbm COPY FURNISHED: ATTY. ANTHONY C.
